name: ODVBench
l2: 在线自动驾驶视频理解
intro: ODV-Bench 是 StreamForest 论文提出的在线自动驾驶视频理解基准。论文 v1 从六个驾驶数据集的1,190段第一视角视频构建6,322道多选题；固定官方发布版本则有6,348行（动态类比论文多26行）。三类场景共覆盖12项实时感知、历史记忆、未来预测与风险推理任务。
org: Nanjing University, Shanghai AI Laboratory, Zhejiang University, Noah’s Ark Lab at Huawei, Yinwang Intelligent Technology
build_method: 六源视频筛选, 双路径元标注, 结构化人工核验, 模板与选项池生成
metric: 论文：12项任务准确率、三类平均与按题总体准确率；固定代码：首个A–E精确匹配，空输出不计入分母
task_type: 在线自动驾驶视频理解, 时空感知, 未来预测
eval_feature: 流式因果约束, 12项任务, 分层准确率
task_type_en: Online autonomous-driving video understanding, spatiotemporal perception, future prediction
build_method_en: Six-source Video Selection, Dual-path Meta-annotation, Structured Human Verification, Template and Option-pool Generation
eval_feature_en: Causal Streaming Constraint, 12 Tasks, Hierarchical Accuracy
intro_en: ODV-Bench is the online autonomous-driving video-understanding benchmark introduced with StreamForest. Paper v1 builds 6,322 multiple-choice questions from 1,190 first-person clips across six driving datasets; the pinned official release instead contains 6,348 rows, with 26 additional dynamic-category rows. Its three categories cover 12 real-time perception, past-memory, future-prediction, and risk-reasoning tasks.
scale_en: Paper v1: 1,190 clips and 6,322 questions; pinned release: 1,190 clips and 6,348 rows; 12 tasks
metric_en: Paper: 12 task accuracies, three category means, and question-weighted overall accuracy; pinned code: first A–E match with blank predictions omitted from the denominator

drawio_review_note: Source-scoped audit reviewed 2026-07-18. The paper contract is pinned to arXiv:2509.24871v1 (the only paper version visible during review), whose downloaded PDF has SHA-256 4ffbc524fed55d020d142bd7597a60b01871df54f46868630b2dd2e52aea7863. Implementation evidence is pinned to MCG-NJU/StreamForest commit f9d14670ff451ff5865638e17c9958e99bf2fec5, the MCG-NJU/ODV-Bench Hugging Face revision 5dcf37ccf7c24ac978db2b8aaad471c0b1b66f21, and the MCG-NJU/StreamForest-Annodata revision ca769c269aee198d9ee6735d85a8c39a699e5833. Paper Section 4, Figure 3, and Appendix C disclose four construction stages: video selection; meta-annotation; QA construction; and quality control. The six named driving sources are ROAD-Waymo, MM-AU, WayveScenes101, BDD100K, BiRViT-1K, and D2-City. OnlineIT is a separate training pipeline, not a source excluded from ODV-Bench construction. Paper v1 discloses neither OnlineIT exclusion from benchmark data nor a cross-set deduplication procedure; instead, the optional fifth training stage uses OnlineIT-Drive to produce StreamForest(FT-drive). Existing annotations and YOLO support candidate filtering before manual video inspection. Strong labels follow direct conversion, while insufficient labels go through VLLM-plus-YOLO coarse annotation and structured human verification. Fine-grained verified metadata is organized into static, dynamic, and event categories with 12 tasks: RTP, PTM, DDM, KIE, HD, TCD, AP, LP, DP, RP, RA, and ARA. Human-authored QA templates and option pools produce plausible distractors with two to four choices; Figure 3 further shows option handling with similar lengths and shuffled order. Multiple manual review rounds and video-length-proportional sampling target task and scene diversity. Paper v1 reports 1,190 unique clips of 5–90 seconds and 6,322 questions at an 18.9-second mean query timestamp: static 247 clips/1,639 questions, dynamic 162/2,973, and event 781/1,710. Direct counting of the pinned public JSON release instead yields 6,348 rows over the same 1,190 videos: static 1,639, dynamic 2,999, and event 1,710, so the release has 26 more dynamic rows than paper v1; the diagram preserves both facts rather than silently choosing one. The benchmark-wide online access contract permits only video content available before the current query timestamp. The paper's 1 FPS constraint is the fixed StreamForest evaluation setup, not a benchmark-wide ODV-Bench contract; Table 1 lists fixed frame counts for offline baselines. The pinned evaluator uses max_new_tokens 16, temperature 0, top_p 1, one beam, and no sampling; it asks for an option letter, extracts the first A–E match, maps it to the candidate index, and reports task/subtask accuracy. Its aggregation skips empty predictions, so its effective denominator differs from a strict all-question paper score, and group-level output does not by itself reconstruct every paper aggregate. Openness is therefore marked partly public: the code tree declares Apache-2.0 and the dataset card declares MIT, but the annotation card says underlying video copyrights remain with creators/platforms and limits use to academic research under relevant agreements. The official evaluator also retains internal pnorm2:s3://OMQA-DS-ALL/ defaults while the README requires users to map videos locally; public metadata and QA rows do not establish unrestricted redistribution of the raw clips. Formal publication evidence [site-a11y-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 4525×561 (English) and 4525×561 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 4523×559 and 4523×559. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
